model_response:

HIV spreads through unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person, sharing needles for drug use etc. There are no specific symptoms of this infection but some people may have fever, tiredness, swollen lymph nodes in neck, armpits or groin area, skin rashes, white spots on tongue or inside mouth, sore throat, painful red bumps on penis or vagina, diarrhea, weight loss, night sweats, muscle cramps, joint pain etc. These signs usually go away within few weeks after which there will be long period without any symptom called as asymptomatic phase. There is currently no cure available against HIV however treatment options exist such as antiretroviral therapy (ART), prophylaxis drugs etc., which help reduce viral load thereby delaying progression towards advanced stages of disease where chances increase significantly leading death due complications related conditions mentioned above.
